name: Link
description: Text that takes the user to another page, another place on the same page, or a file. If the control performs an action on the current page instead, use a Button.
summary: Navigates to another page or location

elements.name: Link text
elements.description: Says where the link goes and makes sense on its own

elements.name: Underline
elements.description: Keeps links in body text recognizable without relying on color

elements.name: Icon
elements.description: Trailing arrow, or an external-link icon with a text alternative

usageNotes: Use <a href> for anything that changes the URL or moves to another place on the page. An <a> without href is not focusable and is not announced as a link.
Write link text that makes sense on its own (WCAG 2.4.4). Avoid "Click here" and "Read more" unless the surrounding sentence or visually hidden text supplies the context.
In body text, don't mark links by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Keep the underline or another visible cue.
A link styled as a button is still a Link: it is activated with Enter, not Space, and screen readers announce it as a link. For actions, use a Button.
If a link opens a new tab or downloads a file, say so in the text or with an icon that has a text alternative. For downloads, see File.
